text:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired for host gpu-node-2147 (zone: us-west-2a). Alert: kernel_oops -> kubelet NotReady. Autopager: escalated to eng-oncall. Pager link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

alice: acked — I'm taking initial lead. Pulling serial console.

sam-sre: on it. can someone confirm if NVMe logs are clean? last few reboots show `XID 79` earlier. will attach dmesg.

ben-ops: reproting from monitoring: node cpu 100% then kernel oops, GPU host lost heartbeat at 12:42 UTC. Affected pods: 12 inference pods (redwood/hosted-modelpool-rt). Metrics: tail latency spiking, 503s for some tenants.

alice: running `kubectl get nodes gpu-node-2147 -o wide` -> `STATUS: NotReady`.

alice: trying `kubectl cordon gpu-node-2147 && kubectl drain gpu-node-2147 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` but drain is hanging due to long-running streaming pods.

jordan-eng: customer impact — two higher-tier tenants (acme-inc, flicker.ai) seeing failing requests, traffic routed to fallback small-model increases cost. P50 latency for embeddings up ~120ms.

sam-sre: serial console attached, past logs show kernel: 'general protection fault' then stack trace. dumping last 200 lines:
```
[  123.456789] NMI: GPU watchdog: GPU-0 hung
[  123.457890] kernel: general protection fault at ...
[  123.458901] task kubelet:......
```

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty escalation scheduled in 5m if unacked by second oncall. :alarm_clock:

alice: if drain won't finish, we should evict by `kubectl delete pod` for the biggest streaming pods then force drain. Starting with inference-pod-xyz.

ben-ops: agree. will start deleting pods on command — prepping the list. tagging team: @sam-sre @jordan-eng

sam-sre: also enabling fallback route in infra-router for model-gallery -> model-gallery-fallback to keep external traffic healthy. patching route now.

alice: performing pod deletes: `kubectl delete pod inference-stream-001 -n hosted-models --grace-period=0 --force` … deleted. repeat for 6 stuck pods.

jordan-eng: notify support: sending status note to acct teams for acme-inc and flicker.ai: "We are performing node failover, some inference requests may be retried. ETA ~10-15m" :email:

incidentbot: Evac check: Node still unreachable via kubelet healthcheck. Kernel oops severity high. Suggested next-step: RMA + repro environment. :wrench:

ben-ops: starting RMA ticket with infra (rack ops). Filling host serial: GPU-SN: G1234-R234. ETA tech on site 2 hours if need replacement.

sam-sre: temporary mitigation complete: fallback route active, most traffic now at stable rates. Rolling back canary is not needed. Monitoring shows 503s dropping from 8% -> 0.7%.

alice: Marking incident in thread for handoff: I'll hand off to night oncall in 20m once RMA ticket is created and we've ensured no regression. Summarizing commands run and logs in ops-runbook.

alice: summary (for postmortem): root cause suspected GPU watchdog -> kernel oops -> kubelet death -> node NotReady. Immediate mitigation: force-evict stuck pods, enable fallback routing, RMA started. Impact: transient 503s for a small set of tenants, increased cost due to fallback. Next steps: collect core dump, repro on test lab, backport vendor kernel patch.

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledgement recorded by alice at 12:45 UTC. Escalation cancelled. :white_check_mark:

sam-sre: leaving notes in ticket: `cores/2147/*.gz` uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/gpu-2147/ . Will request vendor kernel patch after review.

jordan-eng: support update posted. customers notified. closing oncall handoff in 18m. :clock1:

alice: handing over to ben-ops for overnight watch. Ben, can you keep an eye on RMA progress and escalate to platform eng if we see repeated kernel oops on other hosts?

ben-ops: ack. I'll watch and update every 30m or on change. setting PagerDuty maintenance window for host group to limit noisy repeat pages.

incidentbot: thread closed for active mitigation, remains open for follow-ups. tags: kernel_oops, host-failure, RMA, fallback-route
